title: Regular expressions
learningObjectives: Explain regular expressions and use the relevant JavaScript language feature correctly.

understand.concept: A regular expression describes a pattern used to test, find, split, or replace text. JavaScript creates patterns with /pattern/flags or RegExp. Common methods include test(), exec(), match(), matchAll(), replace(), and split().
understand.whyItMatters: Regular expressions are useful for structured text checks, but they are not a substitute for a full parser or authoritative validation. User input still needs clear error handling and server-side validation where security matters.
understand.analogy: A regular expression is a search pattern that describes the shape of text you want to find.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript language protocols, primitive identity, and date/time semantics are defined by the language and runtime.

explain.narrative: The first expression checks a simple identifier shape; the second replaces one or more whitespace characters with hyphens.

practise.guidedTask: Write patterns for a course code and a whitespace cleanup task. Test valid, invalid, and edge-case strings; explain what the pattern does not validate.
practise.independentTask: Build a small example that uses this feature with normal inputs and edge cases. Explain when this feature is preferable to a simpler alternative.
hints: Read the return value and iteration protocol carefully.
Test duplicate, invalid, and boundary values.
Avoid assuming locale or time-zone output is identical everywhere.

questions.prompt: Which RegExp method returns true or false when a string matches a pattern?
questions.explanation: RegExp.prototype.test() checks whether a pattern match exists and returns a boolean.
